title: BBQ Pork Belly Ribs
subtitle: Sticky slow-roasted ribs in smoky glaze
excerpt: Pork belly ribs slow-roasted for three hours until the meat pulls back from the bone, then basted in a smoky, sticky glaze for the final half hour. Low and slow in the oven gives you the tenderness of a BBQ pit without needing a grill. These are best eaten with your hands.
sourceNotes: Barbecued ribs are central to American Southern cooking, with traditions stretching back to indigenous pit-roasting methods; the slow-cook-then-glaze technique became widespread in the mid-20th century as backyard grilling took hold.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze cooked ribs in sauce for up to 2 months. Reheat covered in a low oven.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The ribs can be cooked through the slow-roast stage a day ahead, refrigerated and finished with the glaze in a hot oven the next day.

content.text: Pork belly ribs are cut from the belly rather than the loin and have more fat running through them, which is exactly what you want for slow cooking. Ask your butcher to cut them into individual portions, or buy a slab and slice between the bones yourself. The method is two-stage: a long, foil-covered roast that steams the meat tender, followed by a short, uncovered blast with the glaze to set it sticky and caramelised.
Heat the oven to 160C (fan 140C / Gas 3). Mix the smoked paprika, cumin, coriander and a generous pinch of salt together. Rub the spice mix all over the ribs, pressing it in well.

Arrange the ribs in a single layer in a large roasting tin. Pour 100ml of water into the base of the tin. Cover tightly with two sheets of foil and roast for 2 hours 30 minutes. The meat should be very tender and starting to pull away from the bone.

While the ribs cook, make the glaze: combine the honey, balsamic vinegar, Worcestershire sauce, crushed garlic and chilli flakes in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over a medium heat and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until slightly thickened. Set aside.

Remove the foil from the tin. Increase the oven to 200C (fan 180C / Gas 6). Brush the glaze generously over each rib. Return to the oven uncovered for 20 to 25 minutes, brushing with more glaze every 10 minutes, until sticky, dark and caramelised.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving. Serve with any remaining glaze spooned over the top.

items.symptom: Ribs are still tough after 2.5 hours
items.cause: The foil was not sealed well enough and the meat steamed at too low a temperature
items.fix: Seal the foil tightly and return to the oven for another 30 minutes. Belly ribs need real time and steam to break down.

items.symptom: Glaze is burning before the ribs are caramelised
items.cause: Oven temperature too high or glaze applied too early
items.fix: Cover loosely with foil and reduce the oven to 180C. The glaze should char slightly at the edges, but if it's burning all over, it needs protection.
